quiz.title: Inverse Trigonometric Compositions Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on evaluating cos(tan⁻¹x), sin(cot⁻¹x) and similar compositions with the right-triangle method, plus solving simple inverse-trig equations. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Inverse trigonometric functions — evaluating compositions and solving equations

questions.explanation: Let θ = cot⁻¹(3/4), so cot θ = 3/4, meaning adjacent 3 and opposite 4. The hypotenuse is √(3² + 4²) = 5, so sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 4/5.

questions.q: For real x, cos(tan⁻¹x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Let θ = tan⁻¹x, so tan θ = x = opposite/adjacent. Take opposite x and adjacent 1; hypotenuse is √(1 + x²). Then cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 1/√(1 + x²).
cos(tan⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 + x²) = 4/5 gives √(1 + x²) = 5/4, so 1 + x² = 25/16 and x² = 9/16. Hence x = ±3/4. This is exactly the NCERT Exemplar problem, since sin(cot⁻¹ 3/4) = 4/5.
Let θ = cos⁻¹x, so cos θ = x = adjacent/hypotenuse. Take adjacent x and hypotenuse 1; opposite is √(1 − x²). Then tan θ = opposite/adjacent = √(1 − x²)/x.
Let θ = tan⁻¹(3/4), so tan θ = 3/4 with opposite 3 and adjacent 4. Hypotenuse is 5, so sin θ = 3/5.

questions.q: For real x, cos(cot⁻¹x) equals which expression?
questions.explanation: Let θ = cot⁻¹x, so cot θ = x = adjacent/opposite. Take adjacent x and opposite 1; hypotenuse is √(1 + x²). Then cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = x/√(1 + x²).
Let θ = cos⁻¹(3/5), so cos θ = 3/5 with adjacent 3 and hypotenuse 5. Opposite is √(25 − 9) = 4, so tan θ = 4/3.
tan⁻¹ 1 = 45°, and cos 45° = 1/√2. You can also use cos(tan⁻¹x) = 1/√(1 + x²) with x = 1 to get 1/√2.

faq.q: How do you evaluate an expression like cos(tan⁻¹x)?
faq.a: Set θ = tan⁻¹x so that tan θ = x, then draw a right triangle with opposite x and adjacent 1. The hypotenuse is √(1 + x²), and you read off whichever ratio you need — here cos θ = 1/√(1 + x²).
cot⁻¹(3/4) is the angle whose cotangent is 3/4, so adjacent 3 and opposite 4. The hypotenuse is √(3² + 4²) = 5, giving sin = opposite/hypotenuse = 4/5. It is the classic 3-4-5 triangle.

faq.q: What is the final answer to cos(tan⁻¹x) = sin(cot⁻¹(3/4))?
faq.a: The right side is 4/5, so 1/√(1 + x²) = 4/5. Squaring gives 1 + x² = 25/16, so x² = 9/16 and x = ±3/4. Both values are valid because cos(tan⁻¹x) is even in x.

faq.q: When should I keep both signs of the answer?
faq.a: Keep both when the expression is even in x, like cos(tan⁻¹x), because it gives the same value for x and −x. If a later condition restricts the domain (for example x must be positive), then discard the sign that fails it.
